$comment: MCP tool contract for `decide`. inputSchema/outputSchema are what the server advertises in its tool catalog. Scored single pass over >=2 options; the server argmax-picks the winner and derives confidence from the score margin. The model never asserts the choice. BASELINE, captured from the derived schemas at 038 rather than authored ahead of the code - this tool shipped without a contract, so there is no earlier statement of intent to restore. Its value starts now: any change to the Rust types fails the contract test until this file is updated deliberately.
name: decide

inputSchema.description: Tool input: the decision, the candidate options (≥2), and optional context.

context.description: Optional neutral context/criteria — the only extra subject input.

decision.description: The question to settle, stated neutrally.

anyOf.description:
How much reasoning a call site should spend (022).

Maps to the provider's `output_config.effort`. It governs *all* output
tokens, thinking included, and is a behavioural signal rather than a hard
token budget — `MAX_TOKENS` remains the ceiling.

Unset is not `High`: an unset call site sends no `effort` field at all, so
the request body is byte-identical to before this feature. The provider's
own default is `high`, so unset and `High` behave the same, but only unset
is provably unchanged on the wire.

oneOf.description: Minimal reasoning; thinking skipped on simple tasks.
Moderate reasoning; thinking may be skipped on simple queries.
Deep reasoning on complex tasks. The provider's default.
Always thinks, no constraint on depth.
Always thinks deeply, with extended exploration.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort for this call alone. Omit to use the deployment's
configured level. Not every model family accepts this; when one rejects
it the error names the model, the level, and the remedies.

Typed rather than a free string so the accepted levels appear in the
published schema — the consumer of this server is a model reading that
schema, and a prose-only list is not something it can be constrained by.

options.description:
The candidate options — at least two. Order is the index basis for the
per-option score arrays. May be omitted when `options_text` is supplied.

options_text.description:
Options as a single newline-delimited string (one per line) — an alternative to the `options`
array for clients that cannot reliably serialize a multi-element array argument. Used when
`options` is empty.

inputSchema.title: DecideParams

OptionAssessment.description:
One option's server-assembled assessment — the model's score and rationale
paired with the option label.

outputSchema.description:
The aggregated tool output (data-model.md) — the server-derived recommendation
with its scored rationale. No verdict, no next step.

assessments.description: The full per-option breakdown, in input order (for audit).

confidence.description: Confidence, server-derived from the score margin (`[0.5, 1.0]`).

oneOf.description: The decision turns on several named criteria.
The decision turns on what each option causes or prevents.
The decision turns on uncertainty about which outcome obtains.

runner_up_reason.description: Why the runner-up lost (server-composed: margin + its rationale).

outputSchema.title: DecideResult
